bg_facts: Binance reopened withdrawals in phases on Nov 1.
It says about 95% of stolen assets are replaced.

slides.title: Withdrawals are *back*
slides.body: On Sunday, Nov 1, Binance began reopening withdrawals in phases, three days after hackers took about $6.3 billion. The first window ran 06:00 to 09:00 UTC, with bitcoin going first.

slides.title: Phase *one*
slides.body: Phase one covers BTC, ETH, USDT, USDC, BNB and XRP across 15 networks. Each network must pass its own security checks, so they open one by one. There is no date yet for later phases.

slides.title: The money *now*
slides.body: Binance says it has replaced about 95% of the stolen assets, up from 90% on Oct 31 and about 80% before that. The last 5% is smaller tokens that take longer to buy.

slides.title: Who *pays*
slides.body: The money comes from Binance's own treasury, part of its futures insurance fund and its SAFU emergency fund. Binance says the losses will not be passed on to users and plans to refill SAFU to about $1 billion.

slides.title: Who is *behind it*
slides.body: The FBI says North Korea was behind the hack. Blockchain firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis name TraderTraitor, a North Korea linked group. Binance says its investigation is still open.

slides.title: What it means *for you*
slides.body: If you hold crypto on Binance, check the withdrawal page for your coin and network before you send. Binance said a full proof of reserves would come by Nov 3. Anyone offering to recover your crypto for a fee is a scam.
